controllers.name: fixed_time
controllers.label: Fixed-time (90 s)
controllers.description: Same timing every 90 s cycle, 50/50 split, no coordination. Our starting point.

controllers.name: coordinated
controllers.label: Coordinated (green wave)
controllers.description: Fixed-time with offsets so eastbound platoons meet green at each junction.

controllers.name: actuated
controllers.label: Actuated (gap-out / max-out)
controllers.description: Extends the green while the loop detectors still see cars arriving; switches after a gap of more than 3 s or at max green (50 s), and only if the other street has cars.

controllers.name: max_pressure
controllers.label: Max-pressure
controllers.description: Every 5 s, gives green to the axis with the larger pressure (cars upstream minus cars downstream, from loop detectors). No timing plan needed.

controllers.name: max_pressure_probe
controllers.label: Max-pressure (navigation probes, no defense)
controllers.description: Max-pressure fed only by navigation-app probe reports, trusted blindly. Start the fake-data attack to see it fooled; max_pressure with source=probe, defense=True is the fix.

controllers.name: ai_recommender
controllers.label: AI recommender (engineer approves)
controllers.description: Learns demand from navigation-app probes only, searches a better timing plan in simulation (Optuna), and applies it after an engineer approves — like Google's Project Green Light.

controllers.name: rl
controllers.label: Reinforcement learning (Q-table)
controllers.description: Tabular Q-learning trained on rush hour: every 5 s each junction keeps or switches its green from detector queues; one shared policy, safety stays with the supervisor.

controllers.name: max_pressure_probe+defense
controllers.label: Max-pressure on nav data + detector cross-check
controllers.description: Max-pressure fed only by navigation-app probe reports, trusted blindly. Start the fake-data attack to see it fooled; max_pressure with source=probe, defense=True is the fix.

scenarios.name: rush_hour
scenarios.title: Baseline · Rush hour
scenarios.description: Morning peak toward downtown: heavy eastbound arterial traffic that ramps up, peaks for 25 minutes and eases off, lighter westbound, and cross streets of different sizes. Fixed-time control builds real queues here; adaptive control has room to win.
scenarios.question: How much delay, stopping and queueing does each controller cause in normal peak traffic?

scenarios.name: off_peak
scenarios.title: Night · Light traffic
scenarios.description: Light, balanced night traffic with more trucks. A fixed 90 s cycle makes drivers wait at empty junctions; detector-actuated control should cut delay and stops the most.
scenarios.question: Does the controller stop wasting green time when the roads are nearly empty?

scenarios.name: special_event
scenarios.title: Special event · Stadium lets out
scenarios.title_ko: 대형 행사 · 경기 종료 후 퇴장
scenarios.description: Evening traffic, then the stadium garage north of J3 empties: about 680 extra veh/h leave onto the one-lane cross street into J3 for half an hour (cars wait in the garage when the street is full). A good controller gives J3's north–south phase more green without starving the arterial.
scenarios.question: Can the signals absorb a sudden surge on one cross street, and how far does its queue reach?

scenarios.name: emergency
scenarios.title: Emergency vehicle priority
scenarios.description: Ten ambulances and fire trucks cross the corridor during rush hour from every side: both ways along the arterial, along each cross street, and with turns. Signals give them a green path; we measure their travel time and the extra delay for everyone else.
scenarios.question: How many seconds does signal preemption save an emergency vehicle, and what does it cost other traffic?

scenarios.name: road_closure
scenarios.title: Disaster road closure (flood)
scenarios.description: A flash flood closes the eastbound arterial between J2 and J3 for 30 minutes of the peak. Traffic detours over the back street (J2 → N2 → N3 → J3, or earlier via N1); navigation-app users re-route on live travel times and 30 % of the regional eastbound through traffic avoids the corridor. We measure how far and how long congestion spreads and how fast it recovers.
scenarios.question: How far and how long does congestion spread when the arterial floods, and how fast does it recover?

scenarios.name: sinkhole_cross
scenarios.title: Sinkhole on a cross street
scenarios.description: A sinkhole closes the cross street north of J2 (J2 ↔ N2, both directions) for 30 minutes. North–south traffic at J2 detours through J1 or J3 and the back street, adding turning traffic at the neighbouring junctions — a test of spillover between intersections.
scenarios.question: When one cross street is cut, does the extra turning traffic spill over to the neighbouring junctions?

scenarios.name: earthquake
scenarios.title: Earthquake · closures and emergency response
scenarios.title_ko: 지진 · 다중 도로 통제와 긴급 출동
scenarios.description: An earthquake at t = 1200 s damages the J3–J4 bridge (closed both ways until inspected at 3000 s) and drops debris on the cross street north of J1 (closed until 3600 s). Seven ambulances and fire trucks are dispatched from all sides and must find open routes, while lighter-than-peak traffic detours over the back street.
scenarios.question: With several roads cut at once, do emergency vehicles still get through fast, and does the network recover?

scenarios.name: fake_data_attack
scenarios.title: Security test · fake navigation data
scenarios.description: Like the 2020 Berlin case (99 phones in a handcart faked a jam on Google Maps), phantom probe reports claim a long queue on J2's north approach during the peak. Does a probe-based controller get fooled, and does the cross-check against loop detectors catch it?
scenarios.question: Does fake probe data make a controller waste green time, and is it detected?

emergency_routes.label: From S4, then west on the arterial (S4 → W0)

runs.note: Ten ambulances and fire trucks cross the corridor; signals give them a green path.
runs.note_ko: 구급차와 소방차 10대가 구간을 지나가고, 신호가 녹색 길을 열어 줘요.

runs.note_ko: 기준: 교통량과 상관없이 매 90초 같은 신호예요.

runs.note: Green to the axis with the biggest queue imbalance: about 59 % less delay than fixed-time in our tests.
runs.note_ko: 대기열 차이가 가장 큰 방향에 녹색을 줘요. 우리 실험에서 고정 신호보다 지연이 약 59% 줄었어요.

runs.note: The AI proposes a plan at 10:00 from navigation data; in this recording the engineer approves it a minute later.
runs.note_ko: AI가 10:00에 내비 데이터로 신호 계획을 제안하고, 이 녹화에서는 엔지니어가 1분 뒤에 승인해요.

runs.note: Q-learning controller trained in SUMO on rush hour.
runs.note_ko: SUMO에서 출퇴근 교통으로 학습한 Q-러닝 제어예요.

runs.note: A flood closes the arterial J2 → J3 at 25:00 for 30 min; traffic detours over the back street.

runs.note: The RL controller, trained only on rush hour, struggles once the flood changes the network.
runs.note_ko: 출퇴근만 학습한 강화학습 제어는 침수로 도로망이 바뀌자 크게 흔들려요.

runs.note: A sinkhole cuts the cross street north of J2; turning traffic moves to J1 and J3.
runs.note_ko: 싱크홀로 J2 북쪽 교차 도로가 끊기고, 회전 교통이 J1과 J3로 몰려요.

runs.note: A damaged bridge and debris close two roads while seven emergency vehicles respond.
runs.note_ko: 다리 손상과 잔해로 도로 두 곳이 막힌 가운데 긴급차량 7대가 출동해요.

runs.note: A stadium north of J3 empties onto one cross street.
runs.note_ko: J3 북쪽 경기장의 차량이 한꺼번에 교차 도로로 쏟아져 나와요.

runs.note: 99 phantom phones report a jam at J2 north; a controller that trusts navigation data falls for it.
runs.note_ko: 가짜 휴대폰 99대가 J2 북쪽에 정체를 보고하고, 내비 데이터만 믿는 제어가 속아 넘어가요.

runs.note: Same attack, but probe queues are cross-checked against the loop detectors: the fake jam is flagged and ignored.
runs.note_ko: 같은 공격이지만 내비 데이터를 루프 감지기와 교차검증해서 가짜 정체를 잡아내고 무시해요.
